newsitem.title: PERU: Regional, political worries push Lima shrs down.
newsitem.headline: Regional, political worries push Lima shrs down.

text.p: Lima shares closed lower Friday due to investor nervousness over speculated Brazilian currency adjustments and continuing internal political turmoil, brokers said.
Analysts see a gradual recovery Monday, especially in the brewery and construction sectors, because of good financial reports that will hopefully offset the political problems.
According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index fell 2.96 percent to 2,110.29 points, while the blue-chip selective index also fell 3.52 percent to 3,006.02 points.
The total amount traded was 55 million soles ($20.9 million) in 2,234 transactions. Overall, 12 shares went up, 44 dropped and 30 remained stable.

"Investors are preoccupied by a probable (currency) devaluation in Brazil, which would disrupt the national macroeconomic equilibrium," said analyst Arlen Lahura from Interlima brokerage. "Investors look at Latin America as a whole and have decided to pull out a lot of funds."
Market sources have said that, although the regional influence had the greatest impact Friday, the current political problems plaguing Peru contributed to the fall.

They were referring to, among other things, President Alberto Fujimori's reshuffle of the cabinet Thursday, allegations of phone tapping by the secret services, the revocation of local citizenship from Israeli-born TV station owner Baruch Ivcher and a mass demonstration Thursday towards the presidential palace.
"It is necessary for the president to be clearer...on the political crisis and then we could decide who is defending the economy," said Luis Calderon, from Acciones y Valores brokerage.
Calderon forecast the bolsa will fluctuate next week as investors search for shares with the most profitability, based on the financial data from the first half.

"The mining, construction and banking sectors appear to be the most attractive up to the first half of the year because of the high zinc price, investment in construction and financial restructurings, respectively," he added.

The day's biggest losers were miner Morococha with 10 percent to 7.65 soles, market leader and telecom Telefonica del Peru with 6.23 percent to 6.17 soles and brewer Union de Cervecerias Backus with 4.13 percent to 2.32 soles.
The day's biggest winner was miner Volcan with 10 percent to 18.81 soles and 10.01 percent to 16.49 soles.

Volcan won the purchase of the state-owned Mahr Tunel unit Friday with a $127 million offer and a investment commitment of at least $60 million over five years. Morococha, another bidder saw its shares drop as soon as the decision was announced.
